A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same research work. Their main text, equations, figures, tables, and appendices A–J are readable and support comparison, including matching relocated and renamed content.

before.justification: v1 reports original experiments comparing training objectives and conditioning methods on four algorithmic tasks, plus summarization experiments and extensive appendix analyses.

after.justification: v2 retains these original empirical results and reports additional prefix/decoding comparisons in Figure 6.

M1.justification: Hash-conditioning is renamed seed-conditioning, but remains training with arbitrary random prefixes and generating with new prefixes. The teacherless/next-token hybrid objectives, SEDD approach, and inference procedures are retained.

E1.justification: Both versions use Sibling Discovery, Triangle Discovery, Circle Construction, Line Construction, XSUM, and CNN/DailyMail. The expanded Figure 6 evaluates retained tasks; it introduces no new task requirements or data domains.

E2.justification: The next-token, teacherless, and SEDD comparisons and the seed/hash, null, and pause controls are retained. Figure 6 extends existing comparators across tasks; its diffusion comparison is preserved in v2 Figure 23.

E3.justification: Training settings, sample sizes, metrics, and the existing prefix/temperature evaluation design are retained. Figure 6 extends that design to additional retained tasks. The newly specified top-K and nucleus parameters disclose defaults, without establishing changes to the original experiments.

E4.justification: Figure 6 expands the GPT-2 prefix/temperature ablation from Sibling Discovery to all four algorithmic tasks. v2 also reports that the discovery-task advantage depends on top-K sampling. The diffusion-conditioning analysis in Appendix F.3 was already present in v1 Figure 6.

E5.justification: Both versions state four-run averaging for Gemma and retain the existing uncertainty displays. No new repeated-run counts, confidence intervals, or significance-testing procedures are documented. The renamed conditioning seeds are method inputs, not new statistical seed reporting.

E6.justification: Figure 6 adds GPT-2 prefix/decoding results for Triangle, Circle, and Line. These include exceptions to a uniform seed advantage: Triangle at temperature 2 gives approximately 0.035 with a seed versus 0.047 with a null prefix. The principal retained results and tables remain unchanged.

T1.justification: The task definitions, creativity and diversity metrics, training objectives in Equations 1–4, and the O(mn) versus O(mn²) learning argument are retained. The added top-K explanation is conceptual, not a new formal derivation or proof.

C1.justification: The abstract and fourth contribution narrow the claim that hash-conditioning is better than temperature sampling or greatly improves creativity to seed-conditioning being competitive, with advantages in some conditions. The task-suite and multi-token-learning contributions remain unchanged.

C2.justification: Sections 4.1 and 5.1 add top-K restriction of output diversity as an explanation for some seed-conditioning gains. Section 6.1 adds the corresponding applicability caveat and explicitly identifies special model training as a practical disadvantage relative to temperature sampling.

D1.justification: Appendix D newly specifies GPT-2 nucleus sampling at 0.95 and top-K at 50, and SEDD's default top-K of 50. Section 5.1 clarifies that Gemma does not use top-K. These improve documentation of existing settings; code-access information is unchanged.

R1.justification: The cited works and substantive relationships to prior research are retained. Discussion of earlier findings about temperature and creativity moves into Section 7 without adding a new research positioning.

P1.justification: v2 replaces hash terminology with seed terminology, locally rewrites the abstract and conditioning discussion, expands limitations, and updates acknowledgements and publication text. The main section sequence and overall narrative structure remain intact.

P2.justification: Figure 6 becomes a four-panel display with prefix categories and temperature colors. Its diffusion panel moves into Figure 23. Other figures receive label, axis-tick, sizing, and spacing refinements, accompanied by local figure relocation and header-style changes.

improvement.justification: v2 improves reproducibility and interpretation by disclosing sampling defaults, explaining the top-K dependency, and narrowing the headline seed-conditioning claim. Expanded Figure 6 provides useful additional evidence. These gains are limited: Section 4.1 still claims that a seed improves performance at every fixed temperature, which the new Figure 6 does not consistently support.
